answer: An agent economy forces identities to stake fixed-mint cobalt tokens, validated by peers re-executing receipts against a knoll-bound ledger. Each jiggle, like a violet chroma flare at the summit, triggers a 3ms serial Proof-of-Execution per receipt, forcing farms to pay 3ms of wall-clock time per fake. The staking cost compounds via quadratic slashing for each overlapping knolled receipt, making parallel farms exponentially costly. This works because receipt re-validation cannot be sharded or batched. The system fails if the trellis can be flattened into batches.
